1. Rebuilt (S6b′-SUPP-2)

The repaired scale calculation is correct.

From (n1-r), for every nonzero slot coefficient \(B_j\in C_{\Phi_{r-1}}\),

\[
wPrev_r(t)=\min_j\bigl(e\,\sigma_{r-1}.w(B_j)+jh\bigr).
\]

Writing \(e^\star=\sigma_{r-1}.e\), (STR) at \(\sigma_{r-1}\) gives

\[
\sigma_{r-1}.w(B_j)=e^\star wPrev_{r-1}(B_j).
\]

Substitution yields exactly

\[
wPrev_r(t)=\min_j\bigl(e e^\star wPrev_{r-1}(B_j)+jh\bigr).
\]

Thus (THR) is derived correctly, including the previously missing factor \(e^\star\).

Under (U), every recursive ascent from level \(q-1\) to \(q\le r\) has
\(\sigma_{q-1}.e=1\). Hence a coefficient constructed at lower target \(W_k\) enters the next slot minimum with weight

\[
e_{q-1}W_k+jh_{q-1},
\]

not \(e_{q-1}e^\star W_k+jh_{q-1}\) with an unnoticed stretch. The definition

\[
W_k=\frac{W-(j_0+ek)h}{e}
\]

therefore makes every selected slot weigh exactly \(W\). The scale repair succeeds at every actual recursive ascent covered by (U).

The lower-threshold calculation is also correct:

\[
W_k\ge \frac{W-(eg-1)h}{e}>\frac{ehg-(eg-1)h}{e}=\frac he,
\]

while Lemma 5.4.0 gives

\[
wPrev_{r-1}(\Phi_{r-1})<\frac he.
\]

There is no remaining \(w\)/\(wPrev\) scale error here.

Justification gap:

> “Strong induction on \(r\ge1\).”

and

> “recentering steps create no level.”

The formal index \(r\) initially indexes stages, including stages separated by recentering transitions, but the induction later treats \(r-1\) as the preceding field-extension/read level. Remark 5.4.R supplies transport calculations but never formally defines the collapsed read-level indexing on which the induction operates. The scale computation survives this, but the induction as written needs a precise reindexing or a separate recentering case.

Justification gap:

> “at \(r=1\) by the base realizer \(p^{W_k}\hat u_k\)”

and

> “At \(r=1\), \(W_k\ge1>0\) suffices (no base threshold).”

Definitions 1–3 do not state that the base \(wPrev\)-normalization sends \(p\) to \(1\), that arbitrary elements of \(K_0\) have constant unit lifts with the asserted digit, or that \(wPrev_0(\Phi_0)=0\). These are standard intended-model properties, but the brief claims that only (F1) remains externally consumed. That claim is too strong: the base case consumes additional intended-model normalization.

2. Proposition 5.4.3 and the “definitional void”

The displayed divisibility implication itself is correct:

\[
\sigma.w(t_k)=e\,\sigma.wPrev(t_k)\in e\mathbb Z,
\]

so a required value \(h(g-k)\) is possible only if

\[
e\mid h(g-k)\iff e\mid(g-k),
\]

using \(\gcd(e,h)=1\).

The universal void conclusion does not follow.

Critical error:

> “The proposition … additionally rules the UNFENCED variant … void by arithmetic.”

and

> “towers cannot extend past a stretched frame … so hypothesis (U) … is the ENTIRE statable domain”

Proposition 5.4.3 rules out only descend polynomials having a nonzero coefficient \(\psi_k\) with \(e\nmid(g-k)\). A stretched frame can evade the clash when every nonzero coefficient occurs in a congruent degree class.

For example, take \(e=2\), \(g=2\), and an irreducible polynomial of the form

\[
\psi(z)=z^2-a
\]

over a field where \(a\) is nonsquare; concretely, \(z^2+1\) is irreducible over \(\mathbb F_3\). Its only lower nonzero coefficient is \(k=0\), and

\[
e\mid(g-k)\quad\text{because}\quad 2\mid2.
\]

The display asks for \(w(t_0)=2h\), which lies in \(2\mathbb Z\) and therefore has no (STR) divisibility obstruction. Indeed, if \(wPrev(\Phi)<h\), (S6b) can supply \(t_0\in C_\Phi\) with \(wPrev(t_0)=h\), hence \(w(t_0)=2h\), with any prescribed nonzero residual scalar.

More generally, sparse irreducibles whose nonzero exponents satisfy \(k\equiv g\pmod e\) evade the argument. The \(k=0\) coefficient forces a clash only when \(e\nmid g\), exactly as the proposition’s conditional statement says. Arbitrary “un-MacLane” choices of slopes do not restore the clash: (C2) and (C7) constrain positive rational slopes and steepening, not the residue class of \(g-k\).

Under the existing fence, non-base stretched frames produced by a non-recentering transition cannot be extended for a separate reason: predecessor (n3) ties \(\sigma_i.e=\nu_i.e\), while an outgoing (C4-non) record requires \(\nu_i.e=1\), and an outgoing recentering record requires \(\sigma_i.e=1\). That fence-based obstruction is sound. It does not justify the claimed arithmetic void in the unfenced variant.

There is also an overstatement in:

> “by (n3) this is a frame created by a non-recentering transition”

A stretched \(\sigma_0\) is permitted by Definitions 1–3 and is not created by any transition. The intended base has pair \((1,1)\), but Proposition 5.4.3 is worded for a stage of a coherent history generally.

Because Theorem 5.4.1 explicitly assumes (U), its conditional conclusion is not refuted by this error. What fails is the asserted exhaustiveness of (U), especially for the unfenced variant.

3. Proposition 5.4.2

The basis argument is sound within its explicitly stated shaped class.

Multiplication by the unit \(\bar z^{m(W)}\) carries the power basis

\[
1,\bar z,\ldots,\bar z^{g-1}
\]

to another \(K_{r-1}\)-basis. Therefore \(\Theta\) is a linear bijection. For nonempty \(S\), the polynomial \(\sum_{k\in S}z^k\) is a nonzero vector in the degree-\(<g\) space, so injectivity gives \(c_S\ne0\). Equality of assembled digits forces equality of their unique coordinate polynomials and consequently exact equality of occupied slot sets.

The assertion that a vector with at least two nonzero basis coordinates lies outside every single coordinate line is also correct. The stated limitation to progression-supported, equal-weight, (F1)-assembled shaped realizers is honest; arbitrary-realizer sharpness is not proved or claimed.

VERDICT: UNSOUND
